item.title: Final hurdle awaits RKS
item.description: RATU Kadavulevu School’s under-17 side has one final hurdle standing between it and national glory. After powering past Ba Methodist High School 47-29 in last Saturday’s semifinal, RKS now turns its attention to Suva Grammar School in what promises to be a compelling Vodafone Super Deans Championship U17 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
RATU Kadavulevu School’s under-17 side has one final hurdle standing between it and national glory.

After powering past Ba Methodist High School 47-29 in last Saturday’s semifinal, RKS now turns its attention to Suva Grammar School in what promises to be a compelling Vodafone Super Deans Championship U17 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva on Saturday.

The Lodoni school has travelled a demanding road from the pool stages to the national final, but the semi-final victory also provided a timely warning.

Despite building a commanding score, RKS allowed Ba Methodist back into the contest in the second half — a lapse assistant coach Kemueli Raiqeu knows cannot be repeated against Grammar.

“We had identified some of the weaknesses, especially towards the end of the game,” Raiqeu said.

“We will try and polish them next week so that we can come prepared for next week’s final.”

For RKS, discipline and execution will be the defining factors.

The coaching staff has identified the areas that need attention, with the players now tasked with producing a more complete 70-minute performance when the national title is decided.

“The boys had only one aim today (last Saturday) and that was only to win,” Raiqeu said of the semi-final.

That same mindset will be required against Grammar, with RKS refusing to look beyond the task in front of them.

“We will have to play according to our game plan. Our main aim is to win the final,” Raiqeu said.

The final is also more than a chance to claim national honours. For RKS’s young players, it is another important step towards next year’s international challenge, with the squad already preparing for the Sanix World Rugby Youth Tournament.

But before they can think beyond Saturday, RKS must first finish the job.

The journey from the pools has brought them to the biggest stage — now discipline, composure and execution could decide whether the trophy heads back to Lodoni.

Meanhile, the U18 division final between Lelean Memorial School and Suva Grammar School kicks off at 6.10pm.

item.title: Vanuabalavu embracing Kaji challenge
item.description: VANUABALAVU’S first appearance at the Vodafone Kaji and Kajiana Central 1 Championships is about more than winning games — it is about discovering where their young players stand. The Vanuabalavu under-14 side, made up of players from six schools across the island, is the only team representing Vanuabalavu at the tournament, proudly carrying the hopes of the island and Lau province.
item.content:encoded:
VANUABALAVU’S first appearance at the Vodafone Kaji and Kajiana Central 1 Championships is about more than winning games — it is about discovering where their young players stand.

The Vanuabalavu under-14 side, made up of players from six schools across the island, is the only team representing Vanuabalavu at the tournament, proudly carrying the hopes of the island and Lau province.

The championships began at the Saint Marcellin School grounds in Suva yesterday, with Vanuabalavu opening its campaign against Serua.

They went down 12-0, but for head coach Feresi Dauqito, the result was secondary to the experience his young players are gaining against teams from the capital.

“Our main objective is to expose these young players to the standard of rugby being played here in Suva and see where we stand,” Dauqito said.

“It is also about identifying the areas we need to improve when we return home. This is a learning experience for the players and an opportunity for them to gain confidence.”

For a team drawn from six schools on Vanuabalavu, making the journey to Suva is an achievement in itself.

Dauqito said his players were determined to make the most of the opportunity and represent their island and province with pride.

Captain and fly-half Josefa Magitilailai said his first taste of rugby in the capital had been an eye-opening experience.

“It has been an eye-opening experience for us,” Magitilailai said.

“We have seen the level of rugby here and we know we have to prepare better, stay focused and play until the final minute.”

The 14-year-old also has his eyes set beyond this tournament, with hopes of joining Marist Brothers High School next year.

For Magitilailai and his teammates, the championships provide an opportunity to experience the level of competition they could face as they progress in their rugby careers.

While victory remains an ambition, Vanuabalavu knows the greater reward could come from the lessons taken back to Lau.

For these young players, the Vodafone Kaji and Kajiana Central 1 Championships is not simply a tournament.

They are a measuring stick — and a chance for the only team from Vanuabalavu to show that the island’s young rugby talent can compete on the capital’s biggest stage.

item.title: Sharks gear up for Kajiana showdown
item.description: THE Lami Coastal Sharks are set to make a strong impression at the Vodafone Central 1 Kaji and Kajiana Championships, hosting two competitive Kajiana teams at the Saint Marcellin grounds in Vatuwaqa. Representing the pride of their schools, families, and the vibrant Lami district, the Sharks’ under-13 and U14 Kajiana teams are ready to showcase their skills and determination.
item.content:encoded:
THE Lami Coastal Sharks are set to make a strong impression at the Vodafone Central 1 Kaji and Kajiana Championships, hosting two competitive Kajiana teams at the Saint Marcellin grounds in Vatuwaqa.

Representing the pride of their schools, families, and the vibrant Lami district, the Sharks’ under-13 and U14 Kajiana teams are ready to showcase their skills and determination.

The squads, featuring talented girls from Saint Thomas Aquinas Primary School in Navesi and Marist Convent School in Lami, have trained relentlessly in preparation for the challenge ahead.

Head coach of the U14 team, Phillip Fong, emphasized that while results are important, the main focus is on exposure and experience.

“Exposure is our primary goal for both teams in this competition,” Fong said.

“This championship offers a fantastic platform for our girls to demonstrate their talent against the best teams in the central division.” The Sharks’ U14 team kicked off their campaign with a thrilling win, narrowly defeating Serua 10-5 in their opening match.

For team captain Sarafina Bainivalu, the victory was deeply emotional.

“We didn’t expect to start with a win, but I’m so proud of how the team worked together on the field. We also give thanks to the Almighty for this blessing,” she shared.

For these young athletes, representing their schools and families on such a prestigious stage is a tremendous honor. They expressed heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has supported and believed in their rugby journey.

As the competition continues, the Lami Coastal Sharks are focused on learning, growing, and embracing rugby in its fullest form—with eyes set on returning stronger and ready to prove their mettle in the future.

item.title: Hockey competition shows growth
item.description: THE Fiji Secondary Schools Hockey Competition is proving to be one of the most competitive in recent years, with defending champions falling and new contenders emerging at Nadovu Hockey Ground in Lautoka yesterday. Fiji Secondary School Hockey Association president Makelesi Mawi said 13 schools are competing this year, with three schools from Levuka, three from Lautoka and seven from Suva.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Secondary Schools Hockey Competition is proving to be one of the most competitive in recent years, with defending champions falling and new contenders emerging at Nadovu Hockey Ground in Lautoka yesterday.

Fiji Secondary School Hockey Association president Makelesi Mawi said 13 schools are competing this year, with three schools from Levuka, three from Lautoka and seven from Suva.

Mawi said the tournament had already produced several major upsets, including defeats for reigning champions. In the Under-19 girls’ grade, last year’s champions Suva Grammar School have lost two matches, while in the Under-19 boys, Levuka Public School suffered a surprise defeat to Dilkusha Methodist High School.

With results still unpredictable, Mawi said new champions could emerge when the competition concludes.

Delana Methodist High School has emerged as one of the teams to watch, particularly in the Under-16 and Under-19 girls grades, where they have recorded strong results.

Mawi also highlighted the growth of the sport, crediting the Fiji Hockey Federation’s development programme for helping improve players’ skills.

Development officers are providing training twice during the week and on Saturdays, giving students more opportunities to develop.

“Compared to last year, there is a very big improvement,” Mawi said, noting the number of upsets and draws as evidence of increased competitiveness.

She urged schools and stakeholders to support students interested in hockey, describing it as a highly skilled and safe sport.

Mawi also encouraged young players with an interest and talent for hockey to make full use of their abilities.

She is also calling on school managements to give more students the opportunity to participate.

With the competition entering its final stages with the fight for titles remains wide open, reflecting the growing strength and development of school hockey in Fiji.

The competition continues today with the quarterfinals and semi-finals, following the finals tomorrow.

item.title: St Vincent eye Raluve U16 glory
item.description: ST Vincent College winger Salote Loganimoce says her side is ready for a tough battle when they face Nasinu Secondary School in the Raluve under-16 final at HFC Stadium tomorrow. The 15-year-old from Waibasaga, Wainimala, Naitasiri, played a key role in St Vincent’s College’s dramatic 12-5 semi-final victory over defending champions Sigatoka Methodist College at Churchill Park last week.
item.content:encoded:
ST Vincent College winger Salote Loganimoce says her side is ready for a tough battle when they face Nasinu Secondary School in the Raluve under-16 final at HFC Stadium tomorrow.

The 15-year-old from Waibasaga, Wainimala, Naitasiri, played a key role in St Vincent’s College’s dramatic 12-5 semi-final victory over defending champions Sigatoka Methodist College at Churchill Park last week.

The result ended Sigatoka Methodist’s title defence and ensured a new champion will be crowned in the Raluve U16 competition this year.

Loganimoce produced a moment of brilliance when it mattered most, scoring the decisive try in the dying moments to seal victory for St Vincent’s College.

She said the team was looking forward to the final and had prepared well for the challenge.

“Looking forward to the final. I know it will be a good game and we have prepared well,” Loganimoce said.

St Vincent’s College had to dig deep in the semi-final after falling behind but lifted its intensity in the second half and scored two quick tries to turn the match around.

Loganimoce then delivered the decisive blow late in the match, keeping her composure when the pressure was at its highest.

She said scoring the winning try was the only thing on her mind when she received the ball.

“I’m so happy and when I held that ball, I knew I just had to score that try,” she said.

“I was confident and I thank God for the strength and courage to be able to win it.”

With the semi-final victory behind them, Loganimoce believes St Vincent’s College has the momentum and confidence needed heading into tomorrow’s final.

However, she knows Nasinu Secondary School will provide another tough challenge as both teams battle for the Raluve U16 crown.

For St Vincent’s College, the goal is now simple finish the job and walk away as the new champions.

item.title: Lautoka bids for Western glory
item.description: THE Lautoka Primary Schools Soccer Association is taking a long-term approach to developing young footballers, with a focus on building teams from the Under-10 level through to Under-14. Association president and Tavarau Primary School head teacher Shekar Sharan said the move was driven by the need to develop players earlier rather than assembling teams only when major tournaments approach.
item.content:encoded:
THE Lautoka Primary Schools Soccer Association is taking a long-term approach to developing young footballers, with a focus on building teams from the Under-10 level through to Under-14.

Association president and Tavarau Primary School head teacher Shekar Sharan said the move was driven by the need to develop players earlier rather than assembling teams only when major tournaments approach.

Sharan said the association had struggled to win major competitions in recent years, making player development a priority.

“We have not been able to win for a very long time,” Sharan said.

He said the association had previously relied on bringing players together at the last minute and attempting to prepare them for competition in a short period.

“We’re just bringing the players at the last minute and then we are trying to work on it,” he said.

Under the new development approach, promising Under-10 players are being identified and placed into an elite squad, giving them the opportunity to gain valuable competition experience at a higher level.

The selected players are participating in the McDonald’s Primary Schools Soccer League, which is held monthly for schools across the Western, Northern and Central regions.

Lautoka is represented in the Under-10, Under-12 and Under-14 grades, with players selected from the Lautoka Primary Schools Soccer Championship.

Sharan said the programme was designed to give players regular exposure to competitive football and prepare them for the Western Primary Schools IDC and eventually the national primary schools competition.

The development pathway has already produced encouraging results, with Lautoka winning the Under-10 grade at last year’s Western McDonald’s competition.

However, Sharan acknowledged that the association still had work to do, particularly in the Under-14 category.

“We have not been able to win the Under-14 there,” he said.

The association’s development plan is therefore aimed at creating a steady pipeline of players who can progress through the age groups and eventually strengthen Lautoka’s chances at the highest level of primary school football.

Sharan said the programme also comes with financial challenges, with the cost of running a competition of this size being significant.

item.title: Rugby bodies tighten rules to protect young players
item.description: Rugby authorities have issued a firm warning to agents, clubs and intermediaries against directly approaching school rugby players aged 19 and below as overseas interest in the country’s young talent intensifies. The Fiji Rakavi Football Union (FRFU) and Fiji Rugby Players Association (FRPA) have outlined mandatory protocols governing player recruitment, contracts, scholarships, representation and
item.content:encoded:
Rugby authorities have issued a firm warning to agents, clubs and intermediaries against directly approaching school rugby players aged 19 and below as overseas interest in the country’s young talent intensifies.

The Fiji Rakavi Football Union (FRFU) and Fiji Rugby Players Association (FRPA) have outlined mandatory protocols governing player recruitment, contracts, scholarships, representation and overseas transfers, particularly as the Vodafone Super Deans competition reaches its crucial stages.

Under the directive, agents are prohibited from directly approaching players aged 19 and below, or their parents and guardians, for recruitment, representation, contracts or overseas placements.

Any person seeking to engage a school player must first approach the Head of School, who must notify the FRFU. The matter will then proceed through the appropriate process involving the FRPA before contact with the player or family takes place.

The organisations said the safeguards were necessary because young players and their families could otherwise enter agreements without adequate contractual or professional advice.

FRFU chief executive Koli Sewabu said weaknesses in overseas contracts had previously left players vulnerable, particularly when injuries occurred.

“We have seen cases where players are injured and clubs stop payments because they are no longer playing,” Sewabu said.

“Too many players can find themselves suffering abroad because of loopholes or weaknesses in contracts that were not properly reviewed before they were signed.”

Sewabu stressed that the measures were not designed to prevent players from securing international opportunities.

“We are not blocking opportunities; we are protecting and securing those opportunities,” he said.

Agents seeking to recruit or represent Fijian players will also be required to present their credentials to the FRFU, which will refer them to the FRPA for due diligence.

Players must also submit proposed overseas contracts, scholarships or transfer agreements for review before signing. The review can cover remuneration, accommodation, medical treatment, injury protection, insurance, education, visas, termination provisions, agent commissions and repatriation arrangements.

FRPA director Wame Lewaravu urged families to seek advice before committing to overseas offers.

“Parents naturally want the best for their children, but overseas contracts can contain complex provisions relating to injury, payments, accommodation, insurance, termination and other important matters,” he said.

Players seeking overseas transfers must also obtain their required release before leaving Fiji, with applications lodged after departure not to be approved.

The organisations said their central message was that international opportunities should never come at the expense of player welfare.

item.title: From Ra to the nationals
item.description: Saint Francis College from Rakiraki made a memorable debut at the 2026 Crest Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship in Suva, fielding an Open Girls team for the first time at the national tournament. For team captain and Year 13 student Elesi Sigarara, leading the side at such a major competition was an emotional and proud moment.
item.content:encoded:
Saint Francis College from Rakiraki made a memorable debut at the 2026 Crest Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship in Suva, fielding an Open Girls team for the first time at the national tournament.

For team captain and Year 13 student Elesi Sigarara, leading the side at such a major competition was an emotional and proud moment.

The Barotu, Saivou, Ra native said the team had prepared well and was grateful for the opportunity to compete against some of the country’s best school teams.

“We prepared well for the three-day competition, and we are very fortunate for taking part in the Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship in Suva,” Sigarara said.

Despite the challenges faced in reaching the national championship, Sigarara said the experience had already given the young team valuable lessons.

The captain, who was visibly emotional while speaking about the opportunity, said the team would return home as winners regardless of the final result.

“We faced many challenges to be here, and we want to return with a lot of lessons when we return after the competition,” she added.

Sigarara also expressed her appreciation to those who supported the team throughout its journey.

“I would like to thank my principal, the teachers, the staff members and our parents who are supporting us from the villages, we would like to thank you for your support,” she said.

School principal Dhirendra Nand was also in Suva to provide moral support to the players.

“We have been backing the team with their needs, and I thought it was a need for me to come and provide them the moral support needed,” Nand said.

Nand said the tournament was primarily about giving the students valuable exposure.

“While they have been doing well, result is secondary for us as the primary aim to for them to experience competition as this level,” Nand added.
